title: Plots, Armada and Exploration Adventure
welcome_lead: Today you'll trace Catholic plots, the Armada victory, and the world voyages of Drake and Raleigh.
meta_desc: GCSE History — Catholic plots, Spanish Armada and Elizabethan exploration.
final_note: You learned how plots, the Armada and exploration shaped Elizabeth's later reign.

Raleigh's 1585 colony in Virginia that vanished

walkthroughs.body_html:
Mary Queen of Scots arrived in England in 1568.

Catholic plots followed: Ridolfi (1571), Throckmorton (1583) and Babington (1586). Walsingham, the spymaster, intercepted Mary's coded letters. She was executed at Fotheringhay in February 1587.

In July 1588 Philip II of Spain sent around 130 ships and 30,000 men.

English fire ships scattered the Armada at Calais. Gravelines battered it. Storms in the North Sea wrecked many ships. Only about half made it home. Elizabeth gave her Tilbury speech.

Francis Drake sailed around the world between 1577 and 1580.

He returned with Spanish gold and was knighted on the Golden Hind. Walter Raleigh founded Roanoke in 1585 — the lost colony. England began the slow climb to becoming a sea power.

mcqs.q: Which 1586 Catholic plot was uncovered by Walsingham?
Which colony did Walter Raleigh attempt to found in 1585?
Why was the Spanish Armada defeated in 1588?
options: Elizabeth I personally commanded the English fleet at sea.
Elizabeth reunited England with the Pope to make peace with Spain.
Drake defeated the Armada single-handedly in a great sea battle.
A combination of English tactics and fireships, poor Spanish planning, and the 'Protestant wind' storms that wrecked the fleet on the return.

mcqs.q: What was the Elizabethan Religious Settlement of 1559?
options: Elizabeth I personally commanded the English fleet at sea.
Elizabeth made England fully Protestant and banned Catholic worship outright.
A deliberate via media — a Protestant doctrine and English-language prayer book combined with some Catholic-style ceremony — designed to maximise conformity.
Elizabeth reunited England with the Pope to make peace with Spain.
